transcription.description: The page's text as plain text, transcribed in reading order. Text: always transcribe verbatim, keeping the wording, spelling, punctuation, capitalization, numbers and names exactly as printed, errors and archaic forms included, since readers check the text against the scan and search it for exact terms. Write only text visible in the image and never add, complete or correct anything. Scope: include all visible text, headers, footers, page numbers and tables among it, unless the additional context makes exceptions. Plain text: write the text without formatting, apart from the page-number tags and image descriptions described here. Line breaks: keep each line break where the image has one. Columns: transcribe multi-column text column by column, finishing one column before starting the next. Page numbers: wrap the printed page number of a header or footer in tags, as <page_number>N</page_number>, where it appears; numbers in the body text and in tables stay untagged. Images: describe each image, chart or diagram where it appears as ![Image: description], naming what it shows, its labels and any trend it conveys. Cross-page continuity: the page is usually one of many, so transcribe a sentence that begins on the previous page or ends on the next exactly as far as this page shows it. Use null when the image holds no transcribable text.

no_transcribable_text.description: True only when the image holds no text at all, such as a blank or purely pictorial page; false whenever any text can be transcribed, even in part.

transcription_not_possible.description: True only when the image cannot be transcribed at all, such as a corrupted or entirely unreadable scan; false whenever any text can be transcribed, even in part.
